name: Chinese Chopsuey
steps: Check the noodles are eggless. Bring 2000 ml water and 5 g salt to a boil. Cook the noodles just until tender according to the packet, drain and rinse quickly so they stay separate. Do not fry them: this Chinese chopsuey uses soft noodles. Cut cabbage into bite-size pieces, carrot and bell pepper into thin strips, baby corn into short lengths, mushrooms into slices and onion into thin wedges. Trim the snow peas and mince garlic and ginger.

Whisk the remaining 450 ml water with light soy sauce, rice vinegar, cornstarch, sugar, remaining 2 g salt and white pepper until smooth. The modest soy quantity keeps this vegetable gravy pale rather than dark. Keep the sauce close to the stove because the starch settles quickly.

Heat 35 ml oil in a large wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry onion, carrot and baby corn for 2 minutes. Add mushrooms and bell pepper and cook another 2 minutes. Add garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then cabbage and snow peas for 1–2 minutes; the vegetables should be bright and crisp-tender, not mushy.

Stir the sauce again and pour it into the wok. Bring it to a gentle boil, stirring constantly for 2–3 minutes until it becomes lightly thickened, pale and glossy and coats the vegetables. If the sauce turns too thick, lower the heat and stir vigorously rather than overcooking the vegetables.

Divide the warm, soft noodles among four shallow bowls. Ladle a quarter of the hot vegetables and glossy sauce over each bowl, spreading it so the noodles remain visible around the edges. Serve immediately before the noodles absorb all the sauce.
tips: This soft-noodle, light-gravy Chinese chopsuey follows the source list's description; it is different from red, sweet-tangy American chopsuey and from a crispy noodle nest. Cornstarch must simmer briefly to lose its raw taste. Use a light vegetarian soy sauce, with no fish or oyster extracts.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
